newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes steady, traders ponder Iraq moves.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes steady, traders ponder Iraq moves.

text.p: Cash crude values in the U.S. Gulf steadied Tuesday morning, keeping grade differentials unchanged from the previous session.

Traders said the waiting game for figuring when and how much Iraqi crude would return to world markets remained the feature. U.N. officials said Baghdad has not yet submitted a pricing formula for restarting oil sales, but the move was expected sometime Tuesday.
An Arab diplomat said later that the price plan would likely be submitted "in the next few hours."
Once the price formula is set, then Iraq can lift crude for export after signing oil contracts.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 15 cents lower at $20.55-65 a barrel, with the September/October roll at -10/15 cents.

Grade business saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sell at a steady 24 cents premium to the benchmark. West Texas Sour/Midland failed to budge and was talked at -$1.35/30, and Postings Plus at $1.95-$2.01.
Some dealers see outright crudes were set for a price retreat, as most of the run higher has come on the back of bullish gasoline markets.
